chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said:

I asked him about a man who bought a slave girl while she was menstruating, should he ensure her womb is cleared by another menstruation, or is this one menstruation sufficient for him? He said: No, but this one menstruation is sufficient for him. If he ensures her womb is cleared by another, there is no harm; she is considered as surplus (extra).

key_terms.الاستبراء: Clearing the womb (istibra') to ensure pregnancy status
key_terms.بمَنْزلةِ فَضْلٍ: Considered as surplus/excess (recommended but not obligatory)

ai.seo_question: Is a second menstruation required to clear the womb of a purchased slave girl if she was already menstruating at the time of purchase?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a single menstrual cycle suffices for 'istibra'' (confirming non-pregnancy) of a purchased slave girl, resolving potential ambiguity in early juristic practice. The Imam further notes that performing an additional cycle is permissible but merely a recommended surplus (fadl), not a legal requirement, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical ease in transactional law.
